# Detection models

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_docs.py from the model cards; do not edit. -->

47 detection models. Each section says what the model is, whether it may be used commercially and how fast it is; licences and checks are under Details.

Input: one RGB image. Output: boxes, class labels, scores and instance masks.

Measured on RTX 5060 Ti, torch 2.14.1+cu130; `fastforks bench MODEL --size HxW` measures yours. The summary uses one input, 800x1344: kernels time with its speed-up over the faster original run, and kernels peak reserved memory with its ratio to the smaller original one. Where measured (one variant per family), a variant's table also lists portable under `torch.compile` and the fp16 TensorRT engine of portable ([export](../export.md); memory: the engine's device memory + torch's peak). – = not measured.

Other devices: [Apple M1 Pro 16 GB](../devices/apple-m1-pro-16gb.md), [NVIDIA L4](../devices/l4-22gb.md), [NVIDIA L40S](../devices/l40s-44gb.md), [NVIDIA A10](../devices/a10-22gb.md), [NVIDIA A100-SXM4-40GB](../devices/a100-sxm4-40gb.md), [NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000](../devices/rtx-pro-6000-96gb.md); [across devices](../benchmarks.md#other-devices).

## D-FINE (HGNetV2, N / S / M / L / X)

D-FINE (N, S, M, L, X; HGNetV2, COCO) from USTC: real-time end-to-end detector in the RT-DETR style, 300 queries, deformable attention and box edges refined as distributions, no NMS. Also DEIM (N, S, M, L, X): the same network with SiLU decoder MLPs, trained with dense one-to-one matching.

Commercial use: yes.

### Limitations

- The original in the benchmarks and goldens is the Hugging Face transformers 5.19.0 port (DFineForObjectDetection, ustc-community weights) of the official D-FINE (Apache-2.0); the official repository code itself was not run.
- deim-* variants: DEIM (Huang et al. 2025), the D-FINE network with SiLU decoder MLPs, trained with dense one-to-one matching; weights and the original in the benchmarks are from the official DEIM repository (@09d35d53).

### Limitations

- Requires the optional transformers library (the network is its `GroundingDinoForObjectDetection`).
- The original in the benchmarks and goldens is the Hugging Face transformers 5.19.0 port with the authors' weights (IDEA-Research/grounding-dino-*, openmmlab-community/mm_grounding_dino_*); the official GroundingDINO and mmdetection code (their CUDA deformable-attention ops) was not run.
- Class names are joined into one caption of at most 256 tokens (about 100 short names); a longer list raises an error instead of being split into several passes.
- No phrase output: `labels` index into the given names (the token-level text threshold of the Hugging Face post-processing is not used).
- grounding-dino-base was trained with COCO (and RefCOCO, ODinW) data: its COCO numbers are not zero-shot.

- Original code: <https://github.com/huggingface/transformers> at `c4c4605f9618`

- Training data: WebLI (Google web image-text data, not released), Objects365 (train, box annotations) (Self-training on WebLI image-text pairs with pseudo-boxes from an OWL-ViT annotator (itself trained on Objects365 and Visual Genome), then the weight ensemble of that model and its fine-tune on Objects365 + Visual Genome; Visual Genome has no dataset id here (OWLv2 paper, arXiv:2306.09683; the ensemble checkpoints).)
- Options: `score_threshold` = 0.1 (0.0 to 1.0), `max_detections` = 100 (>= 1), `cuda_graphs` = True (speed only)

| variant | kernels error vs original, mean / p99 | GPU, torch | kernels used |
|---|---|---|---|

### Limitations

- Requires the optional transformers library (the network is its `Owlv2ForObjectDetection`).
- The original in the benchmarks and goldens is the Hugging Face transformers 5.19.0 port with the authors' weights (google/owlv2-*-ensemble); the official scenic (JAX) code was not run.
- Text queries are used as given (no prompt templates or prompt ensembling as in the paper's COCO / LVIS numbers); each is cut to 16 tokens as the transformers processor does.
- No objectness scores and no image-guided (one-shot) detection.
- One box per patch token (3600 for B/16, 5184 for L/14) without NMS, as the original post-processing; overlapping boxes of the same object are common at low thresholds.

</details>

## RTMDet (CSPNeXt, tiny / S / M / L / X; nano and M person detectors)

OpenMMLab's RTMDet (tiny, s, m, l, x on COCO; nano and m person detectors): real-time one-stage box detector, a CSPNeXt CNN with NMS. The person detectors supply the boxes for RTMPose. Apache-2.0.

### Limitations

- The image is resized like OpenCV 4's 8-bit INTER_LINEAR (what mmdetection calls); OpenCV 5 resizes differently by up to two grey levels, so a reference run on OpenCV 5 differs slightly.
- Boxes are not clamped to the image, as upstream: at the right or bottom border they can reach a few pixels into the padding.
- The person detectors' released config names COCO only; the training config stored in the checkpoints (and the file name) also lists Objects365.
